---
title: "Scenario explorer"
---

The paper reports the stress scenarios through a single cross-scenario summary table.
Each scenario, though, produces a full set of exhibits across its whole intensity range
and all four channel-mask arms. This page lets you **pick a scenario and see all of
them.**

### What "intensity" means

A scenario is defined by *which* exposures it impairs. **Intensity** is a homogeneous
gradient along those exposures: at intensity $t$ every targeted exposure is marked down
by the same fraction, scaled so that **1.0 is the scenario's fullest calibrated
stress** and 0 is no shock. Because different scenarios hit different exposures, an
intensity of 1.0 is *not* comparable across scenarios — read each scenario on its own,
and compare the arms *within* it.

```{ojs}
scenarios = [
  {id: "eba", label: "Adverse (headline)",
   desc: "A markdown of the **non-marketable loan book**, calibrated on the EBA 2021 adverse stress-test country projections. Intensity 1.0 is the full adverse calibration."},
  {id: "giips_debt", label: "Periphery sovereign repricing",
   desc: "A mark-to-market write-down on the **sovereign-debt holdings** of Italian, Irish, Portuguese, Spanish and Greek banks. Intensity 1.0 is a total write-off of those holdings."},
  {id: "russia_shock", label: "Eastern-exposure credit",
   desc: "Impairment of **Russian sovereign and credit exposures** together with Baltic, Slovak and Slovene credit. Intensity 1.0 is full impairment."},
  {id: "asian_debt", label: "East-Asian sovereign",
   desc: "A write-down on **East-Asian sovereign debt** (China, Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Korea). Intensity 1.0 is a total write-off."},
  {id: "north_res", label: "Northern real economy",
   desc: "A write-down on the **corporate and household loans** of northern member states (Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, Belgium, France). Because this hits a very large loan book, intensity is capped at a 20% uniform write-down (intensity 1.0); beyond that the exercise is neither plausible nor numerically valid."},
  {id: "south_res", label: "Southern real economy",
   desc: "A write-down on the **corporate and household loans** of southern member states (Italy, Portugal, Spain, Cyprus, Greece, Malta). As for the northern scenario, intensity is capped at a 20% uniform write-down (intensity 1.0)."}
]
viewof scen = Inputs.select(scenarios, {label: "Scenario", format: d => d.label})
```

```{ojs}
md`**${scen.label}.** ${scen.desc}`
```

```{ojs}
maskFiles = ({
  eba:          FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_eba.csv"),
  giips_debt:   FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_giips_debt.csv"),
  russia_shock: FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_russia_shock.csv"),
  asian_debt:   FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_asian_debt.csv"),
  north_res:    FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_north_res.csv"),
  south_res:    FileAttachment("../data/mask_summary_south_res.csv")
})
contagionFiles = ({
  eba:          FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_eba.csv"),
  giips_debt:   FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_giips_debt.csv"),
  russia_shock: FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_russia_shock.csv"),
  asian_debt:   FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_asian_debt.csv"),
  north_res:    FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_north_res.csv"),
  south_res:    FileAttachment("../data/contagion_summary_south_res.csv")
})
```

```{ojs}
mask = await maskFiles[scen.id].csv({typed: true})
contagion = await contagionFiles[scen.id].csv({typed: true})
armName = ({mask_S: "Sales only", mask_SU: "+ Unsecured", mask_SUR: "+ Repo", mask_SURC: "+ CB credit"})
armDomain = ["Sales only", "+ Unsecured", "+ Repo", "+ CB credit"]
maskT = mask.map(d => ({...d, arm_label: armName[d.arm]}))
```

::: {.callout-note}
The **+ Unsecured** arm is drawn **dashed** because it coincides exactly with **Sales
only** once the unsecured market freezes (roughly a third of banks running) — from that
point adding the unsecured channel changes nothing, so the two lines lie on top of one
another. That coincidence is a model result, not a gap in the data.
:::

```{ojs}
// generic line-by-arm plot with the +Unsecured arm dashed so it stays visible
function armPlot(rows, yfield, ylabel, opts = {}) {
  const solid = rows.filter(d => d.arm_label !== "+ Unsecured")
  const dashed = rows.filter(d => d.arm_label === "+ Unsecured")
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 820, height: 360, grid: true,
    x: {label: "Shock intensity (0 = none, 1 = full-scenario stress)"},
    y: {label: ylabel, ...(opts.y || {})},
    color: {legend: true, domain: armDomain, label: "Arm"},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(solid, {x: "intensity_norm", y: yfield, stroke: "arm_label", marker: "circle"}),
      Plot.line(dashed, {x: "intensity_norm", y: yfield, stroke: "arm_label",
                         strokeDasharray: "5,3", marker: "circle"}),
      Plot.ruleY([0])
    ]
  })
}
```

## System equity loss by intensity

Each line is a channel-mask arm; the gap between "Sales only" and "+ CB credit" is the
framework's effect. Loss is on the wipe-to-zero measure, in percent of pre-shock CET1.

```{ojs}
armPlot(maskT, "eq_loss_resid_pct", "System equity loss (%)")
```

## Defaults by intensity

```{ojs}
armPlot(maskT, "n_defaults", "Number of defaults")
```

## Central-bank collateral pledged

How much collateral banks pledge at the central-bank window under the full framework.

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 820, height: 320, grid: true,
  x: {label: "Shock intensity (0 = none, 1 = full-scenario stress)"},
  y: {label: "CB pledged (€bn)"},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(maskT.filter(d => d.arm === "mask_SURC"),
               {x: "intensity_norm", y: "cb_pledged_bn", fillOpacity: 0.25}),
    Plot.line(maskT.filter(d => d.arm === "mask_SURC"),
              {x: "intensity_norm", y: "cb_pledged_bn", marker: "circle"}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## Loss amplification by intensity

The contagion amplification ratio — induced losses as a fraction of the direct shock —
by arm. Lower is better.

```{ojs}
contagionT = contagion.map(d => ({...d, arm_label: armName[d.config]})).filter(d => d.arm_label)
armPlot(contagionT, "amp_ratio", "Amplification ratio")
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Notes
Series are cross-seed means over ten seeds for the stochastic arms (repo and CB-credit);
sales-only and unsecured are deterministic. Intensity is a per-scenario 0–1 gradient
(see above); the real-economy loan scenarios are capped at a 20% uniform write-down,
beyond which the loss measure is not valid. Data are aggregated over the whole 67-bank
sample; no bank-level figures are shown.
:::
